easy.def: A small bit of food between meals.
examples: I eat a snack after school.
The snack is an apple.
We packed a snack.

more.def: A small amount of food that you eat between meals.
examples: I eat an apple for a snack after school.
We packed snacks for the long car ride.
The kids shared a snack at recess.

easy.def: A small, unexpected problem.
examples: We hit a snag.
The trip had a snag.
A snag in the plan.

more.def: A small, unexpected problem or obstacle.
examples: We hit a snag when the bus broke down.
The plan had a snag.
The only snag was that it started to rain.

easy.def: To catch on something sharp.
examples: My coat snagged on a nail.
She snagged her sock.
The branch snagged his shirt.

more.def: To catch or tear something on a rough or pointed thing.
examples: My sweater snagged on a nail.
She snagged her sock on a splinter.
The branch snagged his shirt as he walked by.

easy.def: A small animal that moves very slowly and has a shell on its back.
examples: A snail crawled on the leaf.
The snail is slow.
I saw a snail in the garden.

more.def: A small, soft animal with a spiral shell on its back that moves very slowly and leaves a slimy trail.
examples: A snail crawled slowly across the garden path.
The snail pulled its body into its shell when I touched it.
A trail of slime showed where the snail had been.

easy.def: A long animal with no legs that slides on the ground.
examples: The snake slid away.
A snake has scales.
I saw a snake.

more.def: A long, thin animal with no legs and scaly skin.
examples: The snake slid through the grass.
A snake sheds its skin as it grows.
Some snakes live in trees.

easy.def: To break with a sharp sound.
examples: The twig will snap.
The branch snapped in half.
I heard the stick snap.

more.def: To break suddenly with a short, sharp sound.
examples: The dry stick snapped under his foot.
The rubber band snapped when I stretched it too far.
Ice on the pond snapped and cracked.

easy.def: A short, sharp sound.
examples: I heard a snap.
The snap of the twig made me jump.
The lid closed with a snap.

more.def: A sudden, short, sharp sound like something breaking or closing.
examples: The lid shut with a loud snap.
We heard the snap of a branch in the forest.
A snap of her fingers made the dog sit.

easy.def: Quick and lively.
examples: She has a snappy walk.
The song is snappy.
He gave a snappy answer.

more.def: Quick, lively and neat, or stylish and smart.
examples: The marching band played a snappy tune as it came down the street.
He gave a snappy salute and smiled.
She wore a snappy red jacket to the party.

easy.def: A quick photo.
examples: I took a snapshot.
A snapshot of my dog.
The snapshot is blurry.

more.def: A photograph taken quickly and without much planning, or a short look at a situation at one moment.
examples: I took a snapshot of my friends at the park.
The photo album was full of snapshots from our trip.
The report gave a snapshot of how the town looked ten years ago.

easy.def: A trap for catching animals.
examples: A snare caught the rabbit.
The snare is a trap.
They set a snare.

more.def: A trap used to catch small animals.
examples: The hunter set a snare for the rabbit.
A bird got caught in a snare.
Hidden snares are dangerous to wild animals.

easy.def: To growl and show your teeth.
examples: The dog snarled.
The wolf snarls.
The cat snarled at the dog.

more.def: To growl in an angry way while showing the teeth, or to speak in an angry voice.
examples: The dog snarled at the stranger and showed its teeth.
The grumpy man snarled at us to stay off his lawn.
The cat snarled when the big dog came near.

easy.def: An angry growl, or a tangle.
examples: We heard a snarl.
A snarl of yarn.
The dog gave a snarl.

more.def: An angry growl, or a messy tangle of something such as thread or hair.
examples: We heard a snarl from behind the bush.
I combed a snarl out of my hair.
The yarn was in a big snarl.

easy.def: To grab quickly.
examples: The bird snatched a crumb.
He snatched the ball.
She snatched her hat.

more.def: To grab something quickly and suddenly.
examples: The seagull snatched a chip from my hand.
He snatched the ball out of the air.
She snatched her hat before the wind took it.

easy.def: To move quietly so no one sees you.
examples: The cat sneaks up.
She sneaked into the room.
He snuck out.

more.def: To move quietly so that no one notices you.
examples: The cat sneaked up on the bird.
She sneaked into the room to surprise her mom.
He sneaked a cookie from the jar.

easy.def: A soft shoe for sports.
examples: I wear sneakers.
The sneaker is white.
My sneakers are muddy.

more.def: A comfortable shoe with a rubber bottom, worn for sports and play.
examples: I tied my sneakers before the race.
One sneaker came untied.
Her sneakers squeaked on the gym floor.

easy.def: Doing things quietly so no one sees.
examples: The cat is sneaky.
He made a sneaky move.
A sneaky fox is in the story.

more.def: Acting in a quiet, secret way, often to do something you should not.
examples: The sneaky cat crept up to the sleeping bird.
She gave her brother a sneaky look and took the last cookie.
A sneaky fox is the villain in the old folk tale.

easy.def: To make a mean face or say something in a mean way.
examples: Do not sneer at him.
The boy sneered.
She sneered at the idea.

more.def: To show that you think someone or something is bad by making a face or speaking in a mean way.
examples: The boy sneered at her drawing, which was unkind.
Do not sneer at someone who is trying their best.
He sneered at the idea, but later he liked it.

easy.def: To blow air out of your nose suddenly.
examples: I sneeze when I have a cold.
The dust made me sneeze.
She sneezed.

more.def: To blow air out of your nose and mouth suddenly and loudly.
examples: A loud sneeze echoed through the library.
She sneezed three times in a row.
Cover your mouth when you sneeze.

easy.def: To breathe in through your nose with a short sound.
examples: The dog sniffs the grass.
I sniffed the flower.
She sniffed the soup.

more.def: To breathe in air through your nose in short breaths, to smell something.
examples: The dog sniffed around the yard.
The dog sniffed every bush along the path.
He sniffed because his nose was runny.

easy.def: To sniff again and again, like when you have a cold.
examples: I sniffle when I have a cold.
He sniffled and wiped his nose.
The baby sniffled.

more.def: To sniff over and over, as when you have a cold or are crying.
examples: She sniffled and reached for a tissue.
The little boy sniffled after his fall.
I sniffled all through class because of my cold.

easy.def: A small sniff, or a mild cold.
examples: She had a sniffle.
I have the sniffles.
The sniffle will pass.

more.def: A small sniff, or a slight cold that makes your nose run.
examples: The little boy gave a sniffle.
I have the sniffles and a cough.
Her sniffle meant she had a cold coming on.

easy.def: To cut with small, quick cuts.
examples: I snipped the string.
She snips the paper.
Mom snipped the thread.

more.def: To cut something with a quick, small cut of scissors.
examples: I snipped the string with my scissors.
She snipped a few flowers from the garden.
Dad snipped the tag off my new shirt.

easy.def: A person who thinks they are better than others.
examples: Do not be a snob.
The snob would not play with us.
A snob looks down on others.

more.def: A person who thinks they are better than other people because of their money, clothes or other things.
examples: It is unkind to be a snob and look down on people who have less.
The snob refused to talk to anyone who wore plain clothes.
A good friend is never a snob.

easy.def: To look around where you should not.
examples: Do not snoop.
He snooped in my room.
She snooped around.

more.def: To look around secretly to find out things that are not your business.
examples: Do not snoop in other people's drawers.
He snooped around my room.
The cat snooped in the cupboards.

easy.def: Always looking into other people's things.
examples: The snoopy cat looked.
Don't be snoopy.
We have a snoopy neighbor.

more.def: Always poking around in other people's business.
examples: The snoopy cat looked in every cupboard.
Don't be snoopy about your sister's diary.
A snoopy neighbor peeked over the fence.

easy.def: To sleep for a short time.
examples: The cat likes to snooze.
Dad snoozed on the couch.
I will snooze in the sun.

more.def: To take a short, light sleep.
examples: The cat likes to snooze in the sun.
Dad snoozed on the couch after lunch.
The puppy snoozed beside the fire.

easy.def: A short nap.
examples: I took a snooze.
Dad had a snooze.
The cat took a snooze.

more.def: A short, light sleep.
examples: Grandpa took a snooze after lunch.
The cat had a snooze on the warm windowsill.
A little snooze made me feel better.

easy.def: To breathe loudly while you sleep.
examples: Dad snores.
The dog snored.
I heard him snore.

more.def: To make a rough, noisy sound as you breathe while you sleep.
examples: Dad snores loudly at night.
The dog snored on the rug.
I could hear him snore through the wall.

easy.def: A tube you breathe through while swimming under water.
examples: I use a snorkel.
The snorkel is long.
She wore a snorkel.

more.def: A curved tube that lets a swimmer breathe while face-down in the water.
examples: She breathed through a snorkel while looking at fish.
The snorkel and mask hung by the door.
He cleaned his snorkel after swimming.

easy.def: To swim with a tube to breathe while looking at fish.
examples: We snorkel in the sea.
She snorkeled over the reef.
I want to snorkel.

more.def: To swim at the surface of the water with a mask and a breathing tube.
examples: We snorkeled over the coral reef.
She loves to snorkel and watch the fish.
Dad snorkeled near the rocks.

easy.def: To make a loud sound through your nose.
examples: The pig snorted.
The horse snorts.
He snorted with laughter.

more.def: To breathe out noisily through the nose, often to show an animal's feeling or a laugh.
examples: The pig snorted in the mud.
The horse snorted and tossed its head.
He snorted with laughter at the joke.

easy.def: A loud sound through the nose.
examples: The pig let out a snort.
I heard a snort.
He gave a snort.

more.def: A loud, rough sound made by breathing out through the nose.
examples: The pig let out a loud snort.
I heard a snort from the next stall.
He gave a snort of laughter.

easy.def: The long nose of an animal like a pig.
examples: The pig has a snout.
The dog sniffed with its snout.
A snout is long.

more.def: The long front part of an animal's face that includes its nose and mouth.
examples: The pig dug in the mud with its snout.
The anteater poked its snout into the nest.
A crocodile has a long snout.

easy.def: White flakes of frozen water.
examples: The snow is cold.
We play in the snow.
Snow covered the yard.

more.def: Soft white flakes of frozen water that fall from the sky.
examples: Snow covered the ground overnight.
We built a snowman in the deep snow.
The children caught snow on their tongues.

easy.def: To fall as white flakes.
examples: It snows in winter.
It snowed all night.
I hope it snows.

more.def: To fall from the sky as flakes of ice.
examples: It snows a lot in the mountains.
It snowed for three days.
I hope it snows on my birthday.

easy.def: A ball made from snow.
examples: I made a snowball.
We threw snowballs.
The snowball hit the tree.

more.def: A small ball of packed snow that is thrown in play, or a ball of snow that grows as it rolls.
examples: We made a snowball and rolled it across the yard to build a snowman.
The children threw snowballs at the target.
A snowball grows bigger as it rolls down the hill.

easy.def: Snow coming down, or how much snow falls.
examples: We had a big snowfall.
The snowfall was deep.
A light snowfall began.

more.def: The falling of snow, or the amount of snow that falls.
examples: A heavy snowfall closed the school.
The town gets about two feet of snowfall each winter.
A gentle snowfall covered the garden overnight.

easy.def: One small piece of snow.
examples: A snowflake landed on my glove.
Each snowflake is different.
Snowflakes fell.

more.def: A single, small, feathery piece of snow, which has six points and a pattern that is different from any other.
examples: A snowflake landed on my mitten, and I saw its pattern.
Every snowflake has its own special shape.
Snowflakes drifted down from the gray sky.

easy.def: A figure of a person made of snow.
examples: We built a snowman.
The snowman has a carrot nose.
The snowman melted.

more.def: A figure of a person made out of big balls of packed snow, often with a hat and a carrot for a nose.
examples: We built a snowman with a scarf, a hat and a carrot nose.
The snowman melted when the sun came out.
The children rolled three snowballs and stacked them to make a snowman.

easy.def: Full of snow.
examples: It is a snowy day.
The snowy hill is white.
We played on the snowy field.

more.def: Covered with snow, or having a lot of snow falling.
examples: We played outside on the snowy day.
The snowy hills sparkled in the sun.
A snowy owl swooped over the white field.

easy.def: Warm, cozy and comfortable.
examples: I feel snug in my bed.
The kitten is snug in the box.
We were snug in our coats.

more.def: Warm, comfortable and cozy, or fitting close to the body.
examples: The puppy was snug in a blanket by the fire.
Her snug mittens kept her hands warm in the snow.
The cabin was small but snug during the storm.

easy.def: To cuddle up close and warm.
examples: I snuggle with my cat.
The kids snuggled under a blanket.
She snuggled up to Mom.

more.def: To curl up close to someone or something to be warm and cozy.
examples: The kittens snuggled together in a warm pile.
We snuggled under a blanket and read a story.
She snuggled up to her mom on the couch.
